newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Essendon defender Michael Prior will face severe in-club disciplinary action if found guilty by the AFL Tribunal of racially abusing Collingwood's Robbie Ahmat. The dispute arose during last Friday's game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, and was not resolved during confidential mediation last night. Page 20.

Canberra five-eighth Laurie Daley did the job of two men to steer Canberra to a 30-10 win in last night's Super League match against Perth at Bruce Stadium. The Raiders had to make do without captain Ricky Stuart for most of the match because of a knee inury. Page 20.

New South Wales Waratah rugby players were taken behind closed doors last night by State Rugby Union chairman Ian Ferrier, president Peter Crittle, and chief executive John Winstanley and told their previous fortnight's performances were "totally unacceptble". The dressing down comes after the team's 56-9 thrashing by ACT on the weekend. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian golfer Greg Norman's play-off record fell to a disappointing 5-11 after losing on Sunday to Englishman Mark James at the third extra hole of the Spanish Open at La Moreleja. However Norman has regained the world number one ranking he lost to Amrican Tom Lehman last week after 96 weeks at the top. Page 46.

Proposed changes to Australian tax laws will see nearly all sporting organisations, including many financially strapped Olympic sports, facing a 36 per cent corporate tax rate. Sports bodies last night argued the changes - which would see them lose tax exempt status if they sent teams overseas - would affect their viability. Page 45.

Australian national youth soccer coach Les Scheinflug officially has a job until the World Cup finals midway through next year. However his position is in doubt after the national under-17 team failed to qualify for the first time ever for the world champonships in Christchurch last week. Page 45.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League looks certain to announce soon that this season's state-of-origin match against the Allies will be hosted by Western Australia, probably under lights on Friday 20 June at the WACA Ground. The AFL barred the WA Football Commision from hosting a game in 1996 due to poor attendance. Page B8.

Melbourne Knights soccer player Tom Pondeljak was sore yesterday after a kick to the outside of his left foot left him ineffective in the Knight's 4-1 loss to South Melbourne on Sunday. Pondeljak says he intends to shake off the injury and play in South's return game. Page B6.

Australian jockey Jamie Evans was on a high last month after he won one of England's feature hurdle races at Cheltenham. However, on his return to Australia a week or two later Evans was sporting a broken rib and badly corked thigh. Evans says jump racingwill never be taken as seriously in this country as flat racing. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Former Australian netball captain Michell Fielke is bidding to drive in an all-female crew at this year's Australian 1000 touring car race at Bathurst. Fielke has won two celebrity races at the Australian Grand Prix and recently took a trial drive with Lary Perkins at Calder Park. Page 70.

The Australian basketball side will be captained by South East Melbourne's Sam MacKinnon in the world under-23 championships to be held in Melbourne this August. Mackinnon was elected captain yesterday with Sydney player Aaron Trahair chosen as vice captan. Page 69.

Australian Football League Geelong Cats player Gary Ablett trained at Kardinia Park last night in the first step of his comeback from injury since he damaged his knee in the reserves in round one. It is believed Ablett should be back in only a month. Page68.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The New South Wales government's announcement last week of plans to privatise the NSW TAB could indirectly lead to a resolution of the drawn-out negotiations to televise racing on pay-TV. The racing industry emphasis on its push for wagering taxation refom and TAB privatisation has seen negotiations between Sky Channel and the Australian Jockey Club on hold in recent weeks. Page 66.

The Australian Football League Tribunal last night suspended Sydney Swans player Jason Mooney for four games after he allegedly head-butted Hawthorn's Brendan Krummel during Saturday night's game at Waverly Park. Mooney pleaded not guilty to a charge of misconduct. Page 68.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb finished behind American Nancy Lopez in a tie for second place in the LPGA tournament in Georgia yesterday after a severe thunderstorm cancelled the final round. Webb finished two strokes behind Lopez with Americans Deb Richads and Tina Barrett. Page 61.
